"""Capability model — the *policy* half of the sandbox.

Pure data, no I/O. This is the data model that ``policy.yaml`` in the
agent dir (and later, the ``permission_policy`` component of the bundle)
deserializes into. It is the single source of truth for *what the tool
may do at all* — the fuel/clock/memory limits in ``limits.py`` are the
*how much* half, and ``imports.py`` is the *surface* the guest sees.

The two halves are deliberately separate so that:
- the *validator* (step 1) can check a policy without a sandbox engine
  in the process (policy is data; validation is pure),
- the *sandbox* (step 2) can construct its import surface from the
  policy without caring where the bytes of the policy came from,
- the *portability harness* (step 4) can assert "same policy -> same
  import surface" across drivers without executing the guest.

Concepts (in the order you should read them):

* ``Scope`` — a *single* capability. One capability = one import
  namespace + one fuel-meter hook + one audit hook. Examples:
      - ``fs.read``    read from the *virtual* filesystem the bundle
                       exposes (a named snapshot, not the host fs).
      - ``net.fetch``  a single ``GET URL`` (domain/origin pinned by
                       policy; TLS + method + status code are the
                       observable outputs; headers are stripped).
      - ``clock.now``  logical monotonic time (see sandbox invariant #3).
      - ``random``     CSPRNG, consumed from the host's entropy source
                       and *recorded* (seeded) into the audit ledger,
                       so replays are bit-exact.
      - ``memory.get`` read the agent's own memory_contract fields
                       (the *only* way a tool can read agent state).
      - ``memory.set`` write to them, respecting the field's
                       ``write_policy`` (see artifact.schema).
      - ``emit.text``  append to the tool's observable output stream.
                      This is the only way a tool can "say" anything;
                      there is no ``stdout`` in the sandbox.
  Every capability *must* be explicitly granted, or it is not in the
  import namespace the guest module can see (sandbox invariant #2).

* ``CapabilityPolicy`` — a frozenset of ``Scope``s plus per-scope
  parameters (e.g. ``net.fetch.origins: list[str]``,
  ``memory.set.fields: list[str]``, ``emit.text.max_bytes: int``).
  This is the only parameter surface the guest can *see*; everything
  else (fuel, memory ceiling, wall-clock timeout) is a sandbox-level
  guard in ``limits`` that the guest cannot parameterize.

* The platform *max-capability* file (an operator input, NOT a bundle
  input) is a ``CapabilityPolicy`` whose scopes are a superset of every
  scope the platform is willing to grant any bundle. The validator
  (step 1) checks ``bundle.policy ⊆ platform.max`` before any signing
  happens. A bundle that requests more than the platform max will not
  pass validation, full stop. (This is how the "deny by default"
  invariant gets teeth against a *future* platform that adds new
  scopes: the platform max grows with the platform, not with bundles.)

Validation rules the module must enforce:
- ``Scope`` names are ``"<area>.<verb>"`` (lower-case, dot-separated,
  no wildcards). This is a *namespace* rule, not a regex: the set
    fs.read, fs.write, net.fetch, clock.now, random, memory.get, memory.set,
    emit.text
  is closed, and is the *only* set of valid scopes as of v0.
- No capability names another capability. (There is no
  ``grant.anything`` scope; if the platform ever adds one, the
  validator changes *and* the platform max file is re-audited.)
- Parameter values are *typed and bounded at validation time* —
  unbounded lists are a DoS vector in a sandbox with a bounded fuel
  meter, so the validator rejects them.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum

# Intended surface (now implemented):
#   class Scope(str, Enum): FS_READ = "fs.read"; ... ; EMIT_TEXT = "emit.text"
#   @dataclass(frozen=True) class CapabilityParams:
#       origins: tuple[str, ...] = ()        # net.fetch only, bounded
#       fields:  tuple[str, ...] = ()        # memory.set only, bounded
#       max_bytes: int | None = None         # emit.text only, non-negative
#   @dataclass(frozen=True) class CapabilityPolicy:
#       scopes: frozenset[Scope]
#       params: dict[Scope, CapabilityParams]   # only scopes that carry params
#   class CapabilityViolation(Exception): ...
#   def platform_max_cap() -> CapabilityPolicy: ...   # §5.3 operator input
#
# A *raw* policy name carries the ``agpack/`` prefix (§5.1 spelling), e.g.
# ``agpack/net.fetch``.  :meth:`Scope.from_raw_name` refuses anything without it.


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Bounds (a sandbox has a *bounded* fuel meter, so an unbounded list is a DoS  #
# vector: net.fetch.origins / memory.set.fields cannot name the whole internet.  #
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

#: Maximum number of entries any bounded list param may carry (origins, fields).
MAX_PARAM_LIST_ITEMS = 16

#: The prefix (§5.1 spelling) every on-disk scope name carries.
_PREFIX = "agpack/"

#: The grammar for the part after the prefix: ``<area>.<verb>`` (lower-case,
#: dot-separated, no wildcards).  This is a *namespace* rule, not a regex
#: grant — the closed :class:`Scope` set below is the *only* thing that matches.
_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9]*)*$")


class CapabilityViolation(Exception):
    """A permission policy violates the v0 capability model (§5).

    Raised on *any* structural problem: a scope that is unknown / a wildcard /
    a ``grant.*`` capability, a duplicate scope, a malformed parameter, or a
    parameter that exceeds the bound.  The exception message always names the
    offending scope (or parameter) and the violated rule.
    """


class Scope(str, Enum):
    """The closed v0 capability set — one entry per capability.

    The value is ``"<area>.<verb>"`` (or the bare ``"random"``).  The enum is
    the *only* set of names a policy may name; :meth:`from_raw_name` refuses
    anything else.
    """

    FS_READ = "fs.read"
    FS_WRITE = "fs.write"
    NET_FETCH = "net.fetch"
    CLOCK_NOW = "clock.now"
    RANDOM = "random"
    MEMORY_GET = "memory.get"
    MEMORY_SET = "memory.set"
    EMIT_TEXT = "emit.text"

    @classmethod
    def from_raw_name(cls, name: str) -> Scope:
        """Resolve a raw policy name (``agpack/net.fetch``, §5.1).

        Enforces the grammar + closed-set rules (no wildcards, no grants,
        unknown).  Every name carries the ``agpack/`` prefix; anything else is
        a malformed name.  Raises :class:`CapabilityViolation`.
        """

        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
            raise CapabilityViolation(f"scope name must be a non-empty string: {name!r}")

        # (a) no wildcards — a policy must name capabilities, never patterns.
        if any(ch in name for ch in ("*", "?", "...")):
            raise CapabilityViolation(f"wildcards are not permitted in scope names: {name!r}")

        # (b) the on-disk spelling (§5.1) carries the ``agpack/`` prefix; a name
        #     without it is malformed (grammar error, not a closed-set error).
        if not name.startswith(_PREFIX):
            raise CapabilityViolation(
                f"malformed scope name: {name!r} (every v0 scope is agpack/<area>.<verb>)"
            )
        bare = name[len(_PREFIX) :]

        # (c) grammar: <area>.<verb> (or the bare <verb> of ``random``).
        if not _NAME_RE.match(bare):
            raise CapabilityViolation(f"malformed scope name: {name!r} (expected <area>.<verb>)")

        # (d) closed set.
        try:
            return cls(bare)
        except ValueError:
            pass

        # (e) A name that *looks* like a capability but is not in the set is
        #     almost always an attempt to name a capability-granting capability
        #     (``grant.anything``).  Call that out explicitly — no capability
        #     may name another capability (§5).
        area = bare.split(".", 1)[0]
        if area == "grant":
            raise CapabilityViolation(
                f"{name!r} names a capability-granting capability; none exists in the "
                "closed set (§5) — no capability may name another capability."
            )
        raise CapabilityViolation(
            f"unknown scope: {name!r} is not a v0 capability "
            f"(allowed: {sorted(s.value for s in cls)})"
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CapabilityParams:
    """Per-scope parameters for the scopes that take them.

    A policy's *only* parameter surface (the platform max is separate —
    §5).  A scope carries params only when it appears in the policy and names
    one; scopes without params default to the empty values here.
    """

    # net.fetch: the pinned origins a tool may GET from (closed, bounded).
    origins: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    # memory.set: the memory-contract field addresses the tool may write.
    fields: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    # emit.text: the cap on output bytes for this tool (None = platform default).
    max_bytes: int | None = None

    # -- constructors ------------------------------------------------------ #

    @classmethod
    def from_raw(cls, scope: Scope, raw: object) -> CapabilityParams:
        """Build :class:`CapabilityParams` for ``scope`` from a raw ``params`` map.

        ``raw`` is the ``params:`` mapping from one ``{name, params}`` entry.
        Enforces typing + bounds; raises :class:`CapabilityViolation` on any
        violation (wrong type, unbounded list, negative/absent bound, ...).
        """

        if not raw:
            # A bare scope with no ``params`` key → no params at all.
            return cls()
        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
            raise CapabilityViolation(
                f"{scope.value}: params must be a mapping, got {type(raw).__name__}"
            )

        if scope is Scope.NET_FETCH:
            return cls(origins=_bounded_str_list(raw.get("origins", ()), "origins"))
        if scope is Scope.MEMORY_SET:
            return cls(fields=_bounded_str_list(raw.get("fields", ()), "fields"))
        if scope is Scope.EMIT_TEXT:
            return cls(max_bytes=_emit_bytes(raw.get("max_bytes")))

        # Every other scope takes no parameters.
        if raw:
            raise CapabilityViolation(f"{scope.value} takes no parameters, got {sorted(raw)}")
        return cls()

    # -- accessors --------------------------------------------------------- #

    def has_param(self) -> bool:
        """True iff this scope carries non-default parameters."""

        return bool(self.origins) or bool(self.fields) or self.max_bytes is not None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CapabilityPolicy:
    """A capability policy: a frozenset of scopes + per-scope params.

    ``scopes`` is the closed set of capabilities the bundle is granted.
    ``params`` carries a :class:`CapabilityParams` *only* for scopes that
    actually name one.  This is the only parameter surface the guest can see.
    """

    scopes: frozenset[Scope] = frozenset()
    params: dict[Scope, CapabilityParams] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        # A policy can never carry params for a scope it did not grant.
        stray = set(self.params) - set(self.scopes)
        if stray:
            raise CapabilityViolation(
                f"params for un-granted scope(s): "
                f"{sorted(s.value for s in stray)}"
            )

    # -- construction ------------------------------------------------------ #

    @classmethod
    def from_raw(cls, raw_scopes: object) -> CapabilityPolicy:
        """Build a policy from a raw ``scopes: [...]`` list.

        Each entry is ``{"name": <raw>, "params": {...}}`` — the on-disk shape
        (§5.2).  Enforces the whole rule set (grammar, closed set, no-grant,
        duplicates, typed + bounded params).
        """

        if not isinstance(raw_scopes, list):
            raise CapabilityViolation(
                f"scopes must be a list, got {type(raw_scopes).__name__}"
            )

        scopes: set[Scope] = set()
        params: dict[Scope, CapabilityParams] = {}
        seen: set[Scope] = set()

        for entry in raw_scopes:
            if not isinstance(entry, dict) or "name" not in entry:
                raise CapabilityViolation(f"scope entry must be a mapping with a 'name': {entry!r}")
            scope = Scope.from_raw_name(entry["name"])
            if scope in seen:
                raise CapabilityViolation(f"duplicate scope: {scope.value}")
            seen.add(scope)
            scopes.add(scope)
            params[scope] = CapabilityParams.from_raw(scope, entry.get("params"))

        return cls(scopes=frozenset(scopes), params=params)

    # -- accessors --------------------------------------------------------- #

    def __contains__(self, scope: object) -> bool:
        return scope in self.scopes

    def includes(self, scope: Scope) -> bool:
        """True iff this policy grants ``scope``."""

        return scope in self.scopes

    def param(self, scope: Scope) -> CapabilityParams | None:
        """The parameters for ``scope``, or None if the scope is not granted."""

        return self.params.get(scope)

    def scoped_params(self) -> frozenset[Scope]:
        """The scopes in this policy that actually carry parameters."""

        return frozenset(s for s in self.scopes if s in self.params)

    def as_scopes(self) -> frozenset[str]:
        """The granted scope names as raw strings (``agpack/<area>.<verb>``)."""

        return frozenset(f"agpack/{s.value}" for s in self.scopes)


def _bounded_str_list(items: object, kind: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """A bounded list of non-empty strings; unbounded/ill-typed → violation."""

    if not isinstance(items, list):
        raise CapabilityViolation(f"{kind} must be a list, got {type(items).__name__}")
    if len(items) > MAX_PARAM_LIST_ITEMS:
        raise CapabilityViolation(
            f"{kind} names {len(items)} entries; the policy model caps a "
            f"{kind} list at {MAX_PARAM_LIST_ITEMS} (unbounded lists are a DoS vector, §5)"
        )
    if not all(isinstance(x, str) and x for x in items):
        raise CapabilityViolation(f"{kind} entries must be non-empty strings")
    return tuple(items)


def _emit_bytes(value: object) -> int | None:
    """A non-negative output cap for emit.text (None = platform default)."""

    if value is None:
        return None
    # bool is a subclass of int; reject it explicitly.
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
        raise CapabilityViolation(
            f"emit.text.max_bytes must be an int, got {type(value).__name__}"
        )
    if value < 1:
        raise CapabilityViolation(f"emit.text.max_bytes must be >= 1, got {value}")
    return value


def platform_max_cap() -> CapabilityPolicy:
    """The platform *max*-capability file (an operator input, §5.3).

    Returns a :class:`CapabilityPolicy` whose scopes are a **superset** of
    every scope any bundle may name.  It is never stored in a bundle; the
    validator checks ``bundle.policy.scopes ⊆ platform_max.scopes`` before
    signing.  A bundle may always ask for *less*, never *more*.
    """

    return CapabilityPolicy.from_raw([{"name": _PREFIX + s.value} for s in Scope])

"""Limits — the *resource* half of the sandbox.

What the guest may do *in how much* of the host's time/memories.
Three independent meters, one budget object:

- ``fuel``            — a monotonically-increasing per-run token that the
                        WASM engine charges for every *observable* step
                        (import call, memory growth, loop iteration via
                        the fueled engine). A hard cap per run. This is
                        the meter the audit ledger reads *after* each
                        tool dispatch (not per step — that's too fine;
                        the fuel counter is the host's truth).
- ``memory_pages``    — the WASM linear-memory page ceiling (64 KiB per
                        page in the canonical profile). Growth above
                        this is a *fuel exhaustion* (guest sees
                        "out of fuel"), not a crash — the guest is
                        *supposed* to be able to observe this as a
                        budget failure, not a process death.
- ``wall_time_ms``    — a host-side wall-clock timeout. Belt-and-suspenders
                        on fuel: if the fuel meter itself has a bug and
                        the guest can loop "for free," the wall-clock
                        timeout still kills the run. This is the
                        *last* line of defense and the only one that
                        involves the host wall clock — everything above
                        it is guest-observable.

Design notes:

- All three are *per tool dispatch*, not per bundle run. A bundle run
  may dispatch many tools; each dispatch gets its own fuel/memory budget
  from the *bundle-level* budget the policy declared. The sum of tool
  budgets is what the audit ledger reports as "total fuel" for the run.
  This is the *metering* hook step 5 (the metered-access tool) bills
  against: one dispatch = one billable unit, and the "unit price" is
  the fuel consumed, not the wall time.
- The fuel meter is *the* source of truth for what the guest did.
  The wall-clock timeout is *not* a source of truth — it's a hard
  kill-switch. If a run dies on wall-clock but not on fuel, the audit
  ledger flags it as a **possible fuel-meter bug** (`soft` violation,
  code ``LIMIT_WALL_CLOCK``) rather than silently passing.
- Budget objects are *frozen* after construction; the sandbox engine
  mutates a *copy* it owns (the *spent fuel* counter), and the budget
  itself is what the validator / audit ledger compare against. Two
  different objects, one contract.
"""

# Intended surface (now implemented):
#   @dataclass(frozen=True) class Budget:
#       fuel_max: int
#       memory_pages_max: int
#       wall_time_ms: int
#   @dataclass(frozen=True) class BudgetSpent:
#       fuel_used: int
#       memory_pages_high: int
#       wall_ms_observed: int
#       died_on: Literal["fuel", "memory", "wall_time", "ok"]
#   @dataclass(frozen=True) class Receipt:          # a metering bill
#       fuel: int = 0                                # fuel consumed by a dispatch
#       max_mem_pages: int = 0                       # peak pages observed
#       total_wall_ms: int = 0                       # wall time observed
#   class LimitError(Exception):                     # base of all three
#   class FuelExhausted(LimitError): ...             # fuel_used > fuel_max
#   class MemoryExhausted(LimitError): ...           # memory_pages_high > memory_pages_max
#   class Timeout(LimitError): ...                   # wall_ms_observed > wall_time_ms
#       fuel_meter_bug_suspect: bool                 # True iff died on wall-time but not fuel
#   def check(spent: BudgetSpent, budget: Budget) -> BudgetSpent: ...
#       # the gate: reject (raise) on any over-budget meter, keyed off the
#       # engine's reported cause of death; on a wall-time kill with the
#       # fuel meter still within budget it raises Timeout carrying the
#       # possible-fuel-meter-bug soft flag (code LIMIT_WALL_CLOCK) for the
#       # audit ledger to record -- it does not *silently* pass.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Literal

#: The set of values :attr:`BudgetSpent.died_on` may carry, plus ``"ok"`` for a
#: run that completed within every meter.  This is the *closed* set the audit
#: ledger relies on, so :class:`BudgetSpent` rejects anything else in its
#: ``__post_init__``.
DIED_ON: tuple[Literal["fuel", "memory", "wall_time", "ok"], ...] = (
    "fuel",
    "memory",
    "wall_time",
    "ok",
)

#: The audit-ledger violation code raised (soft, not hard) when a run dies on
#: the wall clock while its fuel meter is *still within budget* -- i.e. the run
#: was not stopped by fuel, which is exactly the signature of a fuel meter that
#: under-counted (see the module docstring).  The gate raises :class:`Timeout`
#: in this case (the run is still rejected) but stamps the soft flag onto it.
LIMIT_WALL_CLOCK = "LIMIT_WALL_CLOCK"


def _nonneg_int(value: object, field: str) -> int:
    """Coerce ``value`` to a non-negative ``int`` or raise ``ValueError``.

    ``value`` is typed ``object`` because a frozen dataclass's annotations are
    *not* enforced at construction -- a bad value can reach here untyped, so
    the runtime guards below are the real contract, not the annotation.

    Rejects ``bool`` (a ``int`` subclass) and floats, because a ``True``
    slipped in as a budget is a silent ``1`` -- the kind of bug the audit
    ledger can never surface.  Zero is a *valid* cap (nothing is allowed).
    """

    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
        # Value/bool/float rejections are intentional as ValueError, not TypeError:
        # the audit-ledger style raises data-class violations, not exceptions, on bad input.
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be a non-negative int, got {type(value).__name__}: {value!r}")  # noqa: TRY004
    if value < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be non-negative, got {value}")
    return value


class LimitError(Exception):
    """Base class for the three resource-limit rejections :func:`check` raises.

    The sandbox treats *any* of the subclasses as "the run hit a resource
    limit" -- a budget failure the guest is supposed to observe as ``out of
    fuel``/``out of budget``, never as a raw process crash.  Catch
    :class:`LimitError` to handle all three uniformly.
    """

    #: An audit-ledger violation code, when this limit maps to one.  ``None``
    #: for the hard rejections; :attr:`LIMIT_WALL_CLOCK` on :class:`Timeout`.
    violation_code: str | None = None

    def __init__(self, message: str, spent: BudgetSpent | None = None) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = message
        #: The :class:`BudgetSpent` that triggered the rejection, attached for
        #: the audit ledger; available to any caller that caught the error.
        self.spent = spent


class FuelExhausted(LimitError):
    """The run consumed more ``fuel`` than :attr:`Budget.fuel_max` allows.

    This is the *normal* budget failure: the guest hit the meter and stopped.
    From the guest's view it is "out of fuel".  The gate raises it whenever the
    engine reports :data:`died_on == "fuel"`, or (when the engine wrongly
    claims completion) the recorded fuel exceeds the cap.
    """

    violation_code = "LIMIT_FUEL"


class MemoryExhausted(LimitError):
    """The run's peak linear memory exceeded :attr:`Budget.memory_pages_max`.

    The docstring frames a memory-ceiling hit as a guest-observable *budget*
    failure (``out of fuel``), not a crash -- and it is, in the sense that the
    guest handles it as a budget failure.  But the host gate attributes the
    cause with its own exception so the audit ledger can report *memory*
    separately from *fuel*.
    """

    violation_code = "LIMIT_MEMORY"


class Timeout(LimitError):
    """The run ran past :attr:`Budget.wall_time_ms`.

    The wall-clock timeout is the host's *last* line of defense -- it is the
    only meter that involves the real wall clock, and it only fires when the
    guest metering itself failed to stop the run in time.  It is therefore a
    red flag for a *fuel-meter bug*: if the fuel meter had counted correctly,
    the run would have hit :class:`FuelExhausted` *before* the wall clock.

    When :attr:`fuel_meter_bug_suspect` is ``True`` the run died on the wall
    clock while its fuel was still within budget -- the gate still raises
    :class:`Timeout` (the run is rejected) and stamps the soft violation code
    :data:`LIMIT_WALL_CLOCK` onto it for the audit ledger to record rather
    than silently pass.
    """

    violation_code = LIMIT_WALL_CLOCK

    def __init__(
        self,
        spent: BudgetSpent,
        budget: Budget,
        *,
        fuel_meter_bug_suspect: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        self.spent = spent
        self.budget = budget
        self.fuel_meter_bug_suspect = fuel_meter_bug_suspect
        if spent.wall_ms_observed > budget.wall_time_ms:
            message = (
                f"wall-clock timeout: observed {spent.wall_ms_observed} ms "
                f"over the {budget.wall_time_ms} ms budget"
            )
        else:
            # The engine reported a wall-clock kill but the numbers say the run
            # was actually within the wall budget -- a contradiction; still
            # reject (the engine stopped it), but do not misstate "over budget".
            message = (
                f"wall-clock timeout: engine terminated the run at "
                f"{spent.wall_ms_observed} ms "
                f"(budget {budget.wall_time_ms} ms)"
            )
        super().__init__(message, spent)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Budget:
    """A per-dispatch resource budget: three hard caps, frozen after construction.

    ``fuel_max`` is the guest-observable fuel cap.  ``memory_pages_max`` is the
    linear-memory page ceiling.  ``wall_time_ms`` is the host wall-clock
    timeout -- the belt-and-suspenders last line of defense.

    All three are validated non-negative ``int``s at construction; ``0`` is a
    valid (maximally strict) cap.
    """

    fuel_max: int
    memory_pages_max: int
    wall_time_ms: int

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        object.__setattr__(self, "fuel_max", _nonneg_int(self.fuel_max, "fuel_max"))
        object.__setattr__(self, "memory_pages_max", _nonneg_int(self.memory_pages_max, "memory_pages_max"))
        object.__setattr__(self, "wall_time_ms", _nonneg_int(self.wall_time_ms, "wall_time_ms"))


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BudgetSpent:
    """What one dispatch actually spent, plus *how* it ended.

    Built by the sandbox engine (host.dispatch) *after* a dispatch returns or
    traps: the fuel counter, the peak memory pages, the wall time the host
    observed, and :attr:`died_on` -- the engine's authoritative account of
    why the run stopped.

    ``died_on`` is validated against :data:`DIED_ON` at construction so the
    audit ledger can always trust it.  ``"ok"`` means the run completed within
    every meter (the default, so the engine can build a happy-path spend with
    one less argument).
    """

    fuel_used: int
    memory_pages_high: int
    wall_ms_observed: int
    died_on: Literal["fuel", "memory", "wall_time", "ok"] = "ok"

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        object.__setattr__(self, "fuel_used", _nonneg_int(self.fuel_used, "fuel_used"))
        object.__setattr__(self, "memory_pages_high", _nonneg_int(self.memory_pages_high, "memory_pages_high"))
        object.__setattr__(self, "wall_ms_observed", _nonneg_int(self.wall_ms_observed, "wall_ms_observed"))
        if self.died_on not in DIED_ON:
            raise ValueError(
                f"died_on must be one of {list(DIED_ON)}, got {self.died_on!r}"
            )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Receipt:
    """A metering bill for one dispatch: what the audit ledger records as spent.

    This is the surface the metered-access tool (step 5) bills against -- one
    dispatch = one billable unit, and the "unit price" is the *fuel consumed*,
    not the wall time (see the module docstring).  It is deliberately a plain
    snapshot of :class:`BudgetSpent` so a billing backend can consume it without
    importing the engine's accounting.
    """

    fuel: int = 0
    max_mem_pages: int = 0
    total_wall_ms: int = 0


def _first_over(spent: BudgetSpent, budget: Budget) -> Literal["fuel", "memory", "wall_time"] | None:
    """The first meter :param spent` overshot :param budget` on, in precedence.

    Precedence is ``fuel`` -> ``memory`` -> ``wall_time`` so the gate is
    deterministic regardless of which order a run overshot multiple meters.
    Returns ``None`` when every meter is within budget.
    """

    if spent.fuel_used > budget.fuel_max:
        return "fuel"
    if spent.memory_pages_high > budget.memory_pages_max:
        return "memory"
    if spent.wall_ms_observed > budget.wall_time_ms:
        return "wall_time"
    return None


def check(spent: BudgetSpent, budget: Budget) -> BudgetSpent:
    """The resource gate: accept a dispatch's :class:`BudgetSpent` or reject it.

    The gate keys off the engine's reported :attr:`BudgetSpent.died_on` -- that
    is the engine's account of why the run stopped:

    * ``"ok"`` and every meter within budget -- the run completed normally, so
      the gate returns :param spent` unchanged.  (If a meter is actually over
      budget despite the report, the gate falls back to the numbers and raises
      the appropriate limit -- an engine that claims completion while it
      overspent did not enforce its own cap.)
    * ``"fuel"`` / ``"memory"`` / ``"wall_time"`` -- the gate raises the
      matching exception, keyed to how the engine said it died.

    On a ``"wall_time"`` death whose fuel was *still within budget* the run is
    rejected (a :class:`Timeout`) and raised with the soft flag
    :attr:`Timeout.fuel_meter_bug_suspect` set to ``True`` -- the audit ledger
    records the soft violation code :data:`LIMIT_WALL_CLOCK` rather than the
    gate letting a fuel meter that under-counted pass silently.

    Raises :class:`FuelExhausted`, :class:`MemoryExhausted`, or
    :class:`Timeout` on the over-budget run; otherwise returns the
    :param spent` unchanged.
    """

    engine_cause = spent.died_on  # how the engine says the run stopped
    cause = _first_over(spent, budget) if engine_cause == "ok" else engine_cause
    if cause is None:
        return spent
    if cause == "fuel":
        raise FuelExhausted(
            f"fuel exhausted: {spent.fuel_used} > {budget.fuel_max}", spent
        )
    if cause == "memory":
        raise MemoryExhausted(
            f"memory exhausted: {spent.memory_pages_high} pages "
            f"> {budget.memory_pages_max} page budget",
            spent,
        )
    # cause == "wall_time": a wall-clock kill.  If the fuel meter was still
    # within budget the run was *not* stopped by fuel, so the fuel meter is
    # a suspect -- flag it.
    raise Timeout(spent, budget, fuel_meter_bug_suspect=spent.fuel_used <= budget.fuel_max)

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import replace

import pytest

from agpack.sandbox.capabilities import CapabilityPolicy, Scope
from agpack.sandbox.limits import Budget
from agpack.trust.delegation import (
    V0,
    ChainHop,
    DelegationViolation,
    DelegationToken,
    _hop_canonical,
    verify,
)
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey


# --- fixtures / helpers -----------------------------------------------------

_RAW_ENC, _RAW_PUB = serialization.Encoding.Raw, serialization.PublicFormat.Raw
_ROOT = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(bytes([1] * 32))
_SUB = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(bytes([2] * 32))

_ROOT_PUB = _ROOT.public_key().public_bytes(_RAW_ENC, _RAW_PUB)
_SUB_PUB = _SUB.public_key().public_bytes(_RAW_ENC, _RAW_PUB)
_KEYS = {"acme/orch": _ROOT_PUB, "acme/copywriter": _SUB_PUB}

_ROOT_AGENT = "acme/orch"
_SUB_AGENT = "acme/copywriter"

_ROOT_TOKEN = "t-root"
_SUB_TOKEN = "t-sub"

_EXPIRES = 9999
_NOW = 500


def _sign(priv, hop):
    return priv.sign(_hop_canonical(hop))


def _base_root_hop(
    *,
    agent: str = _ROOT_AGENT,
    token: str = _ROOT_TOKEN,
    budget: Budget | None = None,
    scope: Scope = Scope.NET_FETCH,
    resource: str = "net.acme/orch.example.com",
    expires: int = _EXPIRES,
    parent: None = None,
) -> ChainHop:
    hop = ChainHop(
        agent_id=agent,
        token_id=token,
        signed_at_unix=100,
        budget=Budget(fuel_max=1000, memory_pages_max=64, wall_time_ms=10000)
        if budget is None
        else budget,
        scope=scope,
        resource=resource,
        expires_at_unix=expires,
        parent_hop_id=parent,
        sig=b"",
    )
    return replace(hop, sig=_sign(_ROOT, hop))


def _base_sub_hop(
    *,
    agent: str = _SUB_AGENT,
    token: str = _SUB_TOKEN,
    budget: Budget | None = None,
    scope: Scope = Scope.NET_FETCH,
    resource: str = "net.acme/copywriter.example.com",
    expires: int = _EXPIRES,
    parent: str = _ROOT_TOKEN,
) -> ChainHop:
    hop = ChainHop(
        agent_id=agent,
        token_id=token,
        signed_at_unix=101,
        budget=Budget(fuel_max=500, memory_pages_max=32, wall_time_ms=5000)
        if budget is None
        else budget,
        scope=scope,
        resource=resource,
        expires_at_unix=expires,
        parent_hop_id=parent,
        sig=b"",
    )
    return replace(hop, sig=_sign(_SUB, hop))


def _valid_token(**kw) -> DelegationToken:
    params = dict(
        v=V0,
        token_id=_SUB_TOKEN,
        iss=_ROOT_AGENT,
        sub=_SUB_AGENT,
        scope=Scope.NET_FETCH,
        resource="net.acme/copywriter.example.com",
        budget=Budget(fuel_max=500, memory_pages_max=32, wall_time_ms=5000),
        expires_at_unix=_EXPIRES,
        chain=(_base_root_hop(), _base_sub_hop()),
    )
    params.update(kw)
    return DelegationToken(**params)


def assert_violation(fn, message) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(DelegationViolation) as exc:
        fn()
    assert message in str(exc.value)


def scope_from_value(value: str) -> Scope:
    try:
        return Scope(value)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise AssertionError(f"'{value}' is not a valid Scope member") from exc


# --- step 1: types closed ---------------------------------------------------

def test_types_closed_v0_must_match() -> None:
    tok = _valid_token(v=V0 + 1)
    assert_violation(lambda: verify(tok, logical_now_unix=_NOW, keys=_KEYS), "version")


def test_types_closed_scope_must_be_scope_member() -> None:
    # a bare string is not a Scope member (and must not be coerced)
    tok = _valid_token(scope="net.fetch")
    assert_violation(
        lambda: verify(tok, logical_now_unix=_NOW, keys=_KEYS), "Scope"
    )


# --- step 2: scope closed ---------------------------------------------------

def test_scope_closed_rejects_unrecognised() -> None:
    # a bare string that is not a Scope member must be refused, never coerced
    tok = _valid_token(scope="net.something-else")
    assert_violation(
        lambda: verify(tok, logical_now_unix=_NOW, keys=_KEYS), "closed Scope"
    )


def test_scope_closed_accepts_net_fetch() -> None:

    assert verify(tok, logical_now_unix=_NOW, keys=_KEYS).token_id == _SUB_TOKEN


def test_scope_closed_accepts_memory_set() -> None:

def test_scope_closed_rejects_missing_key_entry() -> None:
    keys = dict(_KEYS)
    del keys[_SUB_AGENT]
    assert_violation(
        lambda: verify(_valid_token(), logical_now_unix=_NOW, keys=keys),

def test_resource_namespace_closed_rejects_unknown_namespace() -> None:

def test_chain_line_single_hop_root_is_root() -> None:

    tok = _valid_token(chain=(_base_sub_hop(parent=None), _base_sub_hop()))
    assert_violation(
        lambda: verify(tok, logical_now_unix=_NOW, keys=_KEYS), "chain must start"
    )

    )


def test_chain_line_no_cycles() -> None:

def test_hop_signature_must_verify() -> None:

```python
    hop = ChainHop(agent_id=agent.agent_id, token_id=token_id, signed_at_unix=signed_at,
```

```python
def issue_delegation(parent, child, parent_chain, scope, resource, budget, signed_at, expires, token_id):
    hop = make_hop(child, token_id, parent_chain[-1].token_id if parent_chain else None,
                   scope, resource, budget, signed_at, expires)
    chain = tuple(parent_chain) + (hop,)
    # child must be authorized for `scope` under its own policy
    if scope not in child.policy.scopes:
        raise DelegationViolation(f"{child.agent_id} not granted {scope.value}")
    return chain
```

guarantees the door opens" line: the credential is the *signature* (this
agent bundle is who it claims to be); the *delegation token* is the
*authority* — what it's *allowed to do* at this depth in a call chain.

The core data object is a **``DelegationToken``** — a signed, scoped,
time-bounded assertion that "agent X, executing as part of call chain
C, may perform scope S on resource R for at most T time." It is
*not* a free-form JWT (though it *can* be serialized as one for
interop): it is a *structured* token with a *closed* set of fields, and
the validator for it is a *closed* set of checks.

Shape (v0):

    @dataclass(frozen=True) class ChainHop:
        agent_id: str
        token_id: str                    # a stable id for *this* hop's token
        signed_at_unix: int
        budget: Budget                   # the budget THIS hop carried (the
                                          # narrowing link between hops)
        scope: Scope
        resource: str
        expires_at_unix: int
        parent_hop_id: str | None        # token_id of the hop that delegated
                                          # to this one (chain[0] → None)
        sig: bytes                       # the hop's own signature over its
                                          # own (agent_id, token_id, signed_at_unix,
                                          # budget, scope, resource,
                                          # expires_at_unix, parent_hop_id)
    @dataclass(frozen=True) class DelegationToken:
        v: int; token_id: str
        iss: str; sub: str; scope: Scope; resource: str
        budget: Budget; expires_at_unix: int
        chain: tuple[ChainHop, ...]

Two load-bearing design choices:

1. **Issuer is the chain root, not the current hop.**
   The ``iss`` claim names the *root* of the delegation chain. Every
   hop after the root (the agent that delegates *to* me) is a
   *chain entry*, not an issuer. This is deliberate and is the single
   most load-bearing design choice in this module:

   - It makes the token *traversable*. An auditor can walk
     ``token.chain`` from the current hop back to the root, verify
     each hop's signature against the hop's *own* public key (which
     is looked up by agent id in a *key registry*, not in the token),
     and confirm the chain is *connected* and acyclic.
   - It makes *replay* detectable. A captured token from a *previous*
     run of the same agent has the same ``iss`` / ``scope`` /
     ``resource`` but a *different* ``chain`` (different hop
     signatures, different nonces). The validator checks the chain,
     not the token body, so a "replay only the body" attack is a hard
     fail.
   - ``token_id == chain[-1].token_id`` (the current hop);
     ``iss == chain[0].agent_id`` (the chain root).

2. **Resource is a namespaced id, and namespacing is closed.**
   v0 namespaces, one of which the bundle must name:

       mem.<agent_id>.<field_key>
           # a field in the agent's own memory contract

       fs.<agent_id>.<virtual_path>
           # a path under the agent's *virtual* fs

       net.<agent_id>.<origin>
           # an origin (scheme+host+port) the net.fetch scope may hit

   A token that names a resource *outside* these namespaces, or that
   names a field/path/origin the *agent does not own*
   (<agent_id> in resource != token.sub), is a validator *hard error*:
   a token can only delegate over the agent's *own* address space.

Verification (§5 of the spec, fail-fast, in order):

1. **Types closed.** ``v == 0``, ``iss`` / ``sub`` / ``resource`` are
   strings, ``chain`` is a non-empty tuple of :class:`ChainHop`. No
   structural coercion (an integer where a string is expected = hard
   fail, not a policy fail).
2. **Scope closed.** ``scope`` is one of the closed :class:`Scope` set.
   (An unknown scope string is a *hard fail* — there is no
   "future-proof" leniency.)
3. **Resource namespace closed.** ``resource`` matches one of
   ``mem.<id>`` / ``fs.<id>`` / ``net.<id>``. The offending char and
   the namespace name are in the diagnostic.
4. **Ownership.** ``resource``'s ``<agent_id>`` == ``token.sub`` — the
   token may only delegate over the *current hop's own* address space.
5. **Chain is a line.** ``len(chain) >= 1``; ``chain[0].agent_id == iss``
   (chain root); ``chain[-1].agent_id == sub`` (current hop);
   ``chain[i].parent_hop_id == chain[i-1].token_id`` for ``i >= 1``

   does so *at the root*, not at a hop. (Narrowing-only, per the

- No *token issuance* for the root. The root token is *created by the
  bundle*, not by a hop. A hop can *re-issue* a scoped-down token (a
  narrower scope, a narrower resource, or a smaller budget — narrowing

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any

from agpack.sandbox.capabilities import CapabilityPolicy, Scope
from agpack.sandbox.limits import Budget

# The v0 token-format version. Unknown major = hard fail.
V0 = 0

#: The only chain topology v0 supports: a line (index 0 = root,
#: index len-1 = current hop). Fan-out is a v1 spec bump.
MAX_SCOPES = 1  # a token is one-scope, by construction

#: A token names exactly one scope — a multi-scope authority is a
#: *set* of tokens, never one token with many scopes.
_TOKEN_SCOPE_COUNT = 1


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ChainHop:
    """One hop in a delegation chain (a signed assertion by one agent).

    ``agent_id`` is the hop's own agent id (and its signature is over
    the payload, verified against ``keys[agent_id]``). ``token_id`` is
    this hop's token id — the value ``DelegationToken.token_id`` equals,
    and the value ``parent_hop_id`` on the *next* hop refers to.
    ``budget`` is what *this* hop carried (the narrowing link). ``sig``
    is the hop's Ed25519 signature over the *raw* bytes of its canonical
    payload (see :func:`hop_canonical`).
    """

    agent_id: str
    token_id: str
    signed_at_unix: int
    budget: Budget
    scope: Scope
    resource: str
    expires_at_unix: int
    parent_hop_id: str | None
    sig: bytes


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DelegationToken:
    """A signed, scoped, time-bound, budget-bound delegation token (v0)."""

    v: int
    token_id: str
    iss: str
    sub: str
    scope: Scope
    resource: str
    budget: Budget
    expires_at_unix: int
    chain: tuple[ChainHop, ...]


class DelegationViolation(Exception):
    """The token is not a valid, current, in-force delegation.

    Raised by :func:`verify` when *any* of the eight checks in the
    module docstring fail. The message names the specific rule, so a
    failing verify is *explainable* to an auditor (not a single opaque
    "invalid token").
    """


# --- 3. Resource namespace closed-set (v0) --------------------------------

_NSPACES = ("mem", "fs", "net")
_RESOURCE_MIN_LABELS = 3  # "<namespace>.<agent_id>.<rest>"


def _namespace_of(resource: str) -> str:
    """Return the namespace prefix of ``resource`` or raise ``.``.

    Raises :class:`DelegationViolation` with the namespace name and the
    offending char in the diagnostic, per spec §3.
    """

    dot = resource.find(".")
    if dot == -1:
        raise DelegationViolation(
            f"resource {resource!r} is not in a closed namespace "
            f"(expected {', '.join(f'{n}.*' for n in _NSPACES)}), "
            f"no '.' found"
        )
    return resource[:dot]


def _validate_resource(resource: str, sub: str) -> None:
    """§3: ``resource`` is in a closed namespace and names the agent's own space."""

    if not isinstance(resource, str):
        raise DelegationViolation(f"resource must be a string, got {type(resource).__name__}")
    if resource.count(".") < _RESOURCE_MIN_LABELS - 1:
        raise DelegationViolation(
            f"resource {resource!r} has too few labels "
            "(expected '<ns>.<agent_id>.<rest>' shape)"
        )
    namespace = _namespace_of(resource)
    if namespace not in _NSPACES:
        raise DelegationViolation(
            f"resource {resource!r} is outside closed namespaces "
            f"({', '.join(_NSPACES)}); namespace {namespace!r} not recognised"
        )
    agent_in_resource = resource.split(".", 2)[1]
    if agent_in_resource != sub:
        raise DelegationViolation(
            f"resource {resource!r} names agent {agent_in_resource!r}, "
            f"not token sub {sub!r}; a token can only delegate over "
            f"its own agent address space"
        )

{"path": "/home/iconbaypark2900/openworker-tasks/8cc21757-c15/call_chain_demo.py", "content": """"Multi-agent call chain over agpack's *delegation* trust layer.

This is Direction 2 of the agpack demo: not engine-diversity (that was the
portability proof), but *authority-diversity*. The one thing agpack does
that nothing else in the stack does is per-hop scoped delegation: a token
that is *signed*, *scoped*, *time-bounded*, and *budget-narrowing* — and it
narrows as it passes hop to hop through a signed chain.

Three agent bundles walk the same token forward:

    Researcher  --delegates a broad "search + reason" authority-->
      Analyst  --delegates a narrower "write to my memory only" authority-->
        Scribe   --executes as the leaf; scope MEM_SET on its own resource

Each hop re-issues a *narrower* token (scope + resource + budget all shrink);
the root (Researcher) is the only hop allowed to set the widest authority.
`agpack.trust.delegation.verify` enforces, in 8 closed checks, that every
hop's signature is real, the chain is a line, nothing is expired, and the
budget only ever shrinks.

Then, from the audit ledger, we REPLAY the chain: reconstruct the exact
signature path from leaf back to root and confirm `verify` still passes.
A captured-or-forged hop (a tampered signature, or a hop whose scope is
*broadened* relative to its parent) is a hard `DelegationViolation`.

Runtime, no network:
    python call_chain_demo.py

(agpack source is read-only here; the venv under the read-only
.dataScience/agpack/.scratch/venv is on sys.path by the conftest for tests.
Run this file directly to use the installed `agpack` in your own venv, or
the conftest below to drive the read-only source.)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable

# agpack modules — trust (signing + delegation) + audit + sandbox caps.
from agpack.trust.signing import Keypair, sign, verify as sig_verify
from agpack.trust.delegation import (
    ChainHop,
    DelegationViolation,
    DelegationToken,
    Budget,
    Scope,
    verify,
    _hop_canonical,  # canonical bytes the signature is over; public in the bundle
)
from agpack.trust.audit import AuditLedger, AuditRecord, replay as audit_replay
from agpack.sandbox.capabilities import Capability, CapabilityPolicy, Scope as AgScope

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A tiny identity/registry layer. `verify` looks each hop's signature up by
# agent id in a *key registry* — the keys are NOT in the token, they live
# outside it. We model that here with a signing Keypair per agent.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_KEY_REGISTRY: dict[str, Keypair] = {}


def register_agent(agent_id: str) -> Keypair:
    kp = Keypair()
    _KEY_REGISTRY[agent_id] = kp
    return kp


def _registry_keys() -> dict[str, Keypair]:
    # verify() wants something whose .public_bytes is the raw public key for
    # each agent_id. We hand it a small adapter object per key.
    return _KEY_REGISTRY


# Keypair must expose `.public_bytes` — verify() reads that. Confirm the
# shape by inspecting; if it differs, swap in what it actually needs.
_KEY_ADAPTER = type("_KeyAdapter", (), {})


def _keys_adapter() -> dict[str, object]:
    class _K:
        def __init__(self, kp: Keypair) -> None:
            self._kp = kp

        @property
        def public_bytes(self) -> bytes:
            return self._kp.public_bytes

    return {aid: _K(kp) for aid, kp in _KEY_REGISTRY.items()}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hops. Each agent, given the incoming token it is allowed to act under,
# issues the *next* (narrower) token. `scope`, `resource`, `budget` all
# shrink; that is the only thing a hop may do.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _issue_hop(
    agent_id: str,
    parent: ChainHop | None,
    scope: Scope,
    resource: str,
    budget: Budget,
    expires_at_unix: int,
) -> ChainHop:
    """Sign one chain hop. `parent` is the previous hop (None for the root).

    The hop signs its own canonical payload; the signature is the *nonce*
    that binds the chain together — it is what makes replay and forgery
    detectable.
    """
    kp = _KEY_REGISTRY[agent_id]
    token_id = f"{agent_id}:{int(time.time_ns())}"
    hop = ChainHop(
        agent_id=agent_id,
        token_id=token_id,
        signed_at_unix=int(time.time()),
        budget=budget,
        scope=scope,
        resource=resource,
        expires_at_unix=expires_at_unix,
        parent_hop_id=None if parent is None else parent.token_id,
        sig=b"",  # filled in below
    )
    hop = hop.replace(sig=sign(kp, _hop_canonical(hop)))
    return hop


def _chain_from_root(hops: list[ChainHop]) -> DelegationToken:
    """Assemble a token whose chain is the hops from root(0)..leaf(last).

    Conforms to: iss==chain[0].agent_id, sub==chain[-1].agent_id,
    token_id==chain[-1].token_id.
    """
    assert hops[0].parent_hop_id is None, "chain[0] must be the root"
    for i in range(1, len(hops)):
        assert hops[i].parent_hop_id == hops[i - 1].token_id, (
            f"chain broken at hop {i}"
        )
    return DelegationToken(
        v=0,
        token_id=hops[-1].token_id,
        iss=hops[0].agent_id,
        sub=hops[-1].agent_id,
        scope=hops[-1].scope,
        resource=hops[-1].resource,
        budget=hops[-1].budget,
        expires_at_unix=hops[-1].expires_at_unix,
        chain=tuple(hops),
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The call chain.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def run_call_chain() -> dict[str, object]:
    t0 = int(time.time())
    exp = t0 + 3600  # one hour — comfortably in the future

    # --- identities -------------------------------------------------------
    for aid in ("researcher", "analyst", "scribe"):
        register_agent(aid)

    # --- root hop: Researcher, widest authority ---------------------------
    # Scope READ over the whole research address space, fuel budget 100.
    root = _issue_hop(
        agent_id="researcher",
        parent=None,
        scope=Scope.MEM_READ,
        resource="mem.researcher.research",
        budget=Budget(fuel_max=100, memory_pages_max=512, wall_time_ms=60000),
        expires_at_unix=exp,
    )
    root_token = _chain_from_root([root])
    verify(root_token, _keys_adapter(), exp)  # sanity: root verifies

    # --- hop 1: Researcher delegates to Analyst ---------------------------
    # Narrow: analyst may only READ+WRITE its own memory, and only the
    # analysis sub-space. Budget shrinks too (fuel 60 < 100).
    analyst = _issue_hop(
        agent_id="analyst",
        parent=root,
        scope=Scope.MEM_WRITE,
        resource="mem.analyst.analysis",
        budget=Budget(fuel_max=60, memory_pages_max=256, wall_time_ms=30000),
        expires_at_unix=exp,
    )
    analyst_token = _chain_from_root([root, analyst])

    # --- hop 2: Analyst delegates to Scribe -------------------------------
    # Narrow still: scribe can only *store* one field in its own memory.
    scribe = _issue_hop(
        agent_id="scribe",
        parent=analyst,
        scope=Scope.MEM_SET,
        resource="mem.scribe.report",
        budget=Budget(fuel_max=20, memory_pages_max=64, wall_time_ms=5000),
        expires_at_unix=exp,
    )
    scribe_token = _chain_from_root([root, analyst, scribe])

    # The leaf executes under the *fully-narrowed* authority.
    verify(scribe_token, _keys_adapter(), exp)

    return {
        "root_token": root_token,
        "analyst_token": analyst_token,
        "scribe_token": scribe_token,
        "logical_now": exp,
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Replay from the audit ledger — reconstruct the signature path.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def run_replay(scribe_token: DelegationToken) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Replay the chain from the leaf back to root using an audit ledger.

    Each hop, as it was signed, would have written an `AuditRecord` to a
    ledger. Given only the ledger (and the recovered hop chain from the
    token), `replay` re-verifies the signature path end-to-end.
    """
    ledger: AuditLedger = AuditLedger()

    # Replay each hop as if it were being recorded live.
    records: list[AuditRecord] = []
    for hop in scribe_token.chain:
        record = AuditRecord(
            kind="delegate",
            agent_id=hop.agent_id,
            fields={
                "token_id": hop.token_id,
                "parent_hop_id": hop.parent_hop_id,
                "scope": hop.scope,
                "resource": hop.resource,
                "fuel_max": hop.budget.fuel_max,
                "signed_at_unix": hop.signed_at_unix,
            },
        )
        ledger.append(record)
        records.append(record)

    # Reconstruct + re-verify: replay returns the hop chain; verify it.
    recovered = audit_replay(scribe_token, ledger)
    verify(scribe_token, _keys_adapter(), scribe_token.expires_at_unix)
    return {"records": records, "recovered_chain": recovered}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Negative cases: what `verify` *rejects*. Each must raise DelegationViolation.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _expect_rejection(label: str, token: DelegationToken, logical_now: int) -> None:
    try:
        verify(token, _keys_adapter(), logical_now)
    except DelegationViolation as exc:
        return label, str(exc)[:80]

  manifest, then tar.gz's the result. The *entire tar.gz is not

class LedgerCorrupt(Exception):
    """A record fails its own kind's schema check.

    Raised by :func:`replay` (and by :meth:`AuditLedger` construction checks
    when *strict* validation is requested). A corrupt record is *not* a
    malformed-but-acceptable entry — the ledger is self-describing, so a
    record whose ``detail`` does not match its ``kind`` is treated as a
    corruption and rejected, never silently recorded.
    """


class AuditLedger:
    """The *append-only* container the host imports write to.

    ``append(rec)`` adds a record and assigns it the next ordinal
    (unless the record already carries one). Iteration and indexing are
    in ordinal order. The *storage* behind the in-memory record list is
    the caller's job; this module *produces* records, it doesn't
    *store* them on disk.
    """

    def __init__(self, *, start: int = 0) -> None:
        """Create an empty ledger.

        ``start`` is the ordinal the *first* appended record receives; it
        exists so a storage-level truncation-restart (with a
        ``continued_from`` reference, per the module docstring) can hand a
        fresh ledger instance a non-zero origin. Defaults to ``0``.
        """

        self._start = start
        self._records: list[AuditRecord] = []

    # -- append ----------------------------------------------------------- #

    def append(self, record: AuditRecord) -> None:
        """Append one record, assigning it the next ordinal.

        If ``record`` carries no ordinal (the sandbox's
        ``import_call`` / ``dispatch`` / ``budget`` records are built
        without one) the ledger stamps the next ordinal onto it via
        :func:`object.__setattr__` — the ledger *owns* ordinal assignment,
        the caller never does. A record that already has an ``ordinal`` is
        stored as-is (used by callers constructing records out-of-band).
        """

        if not hasattr(record, "ordinal") or record.ordinal is None:
            object.__setattr__(record, "ordinal", self._current_ordinal())
        self._records.append(record)

    def _current_ordinal(self) -> int:
        """The ordinal the next record will receive."""

        return self._start + len(self._records)

    # -- iteration / size ------------------------------------------------- #

    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[AuditRecord]:
        return iter(self._records)

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._records)

    def __getitem__(self, index: int) -> AuditRecord:
        return self._records[index]

    def last_ordinal(self) -> int:
        """The ordinal of the last record, or ``start - 1`` when empty.

        This is the ordinal the next record will *not* reuse — it is the
        "last used ordinal", so an empty ledger at ``start=0`` returns
        ``-1`` (nothing has been appended).
        """

        return self._start - 1 if not self._records else self._records[-1].ordinal

    def records(self) -> tuple[AuditRecord, ...]:
        """A snapshot tuple of the records in ordinal order."""

        return tuple(self._records)

    # -- self-validation -------------------------------------------------- #

    def validate(self, strict: bool = True) -> None:
        """Raise :class:`LedgerCorrupt` if any record fails its kind schema.

        A no-op on a clean ledger; on a corrupt one it names the ordinal,
        the kind, and the offending detail key.
        """

        for rec in self._records:
            self._check_record(rec, strict=strict)

    def _check_record(self, record: AuditRecord, *, strict: bool) -> None:
        if record.kind not in _DETAIL_SCHEMAS:
            raise LedgerCorrupt(
                f"record {record.ordinal}: unknown kind {record.kind!r} "
                f"(expected one of {list(_DETAIL_SCHEMAS)})"
            )
        if not _detail_ok(record.detail, _DETAIL_SCHEMAS[record.kind]):
            raise LedgerCorrupt(
                f"record {record.ordinal}: kind {record.kind!r} detail is "
                f"corrupt (missing/incorrect required field)"
            )


def _check(record: AuditRecord) -> None:
    """Validate a single record, raising :class:`LedgerCorrupt` on failure."""

per-hop scoped delegation — a token that is signed, scoped, time-bounded,
and budget-narrowing, and it *narrows* as it passes hop to hop through a
signed chain. Three agent bundles walk the same token forward:

    researcher  --broad "read the research space" authority-->
      analyst   --narrower "write to my own memory only" authority-->
        scribe  --leaf: only store one field in its own memory

The root (researcher) sets the widest authority; each hop may *only narrow*
(scope + resource + budget all shrink). `agpack.trust.delegation.verify`
enforces, in eight closed checks, that every hop's signature is real, the
chain is a line, nothing is expired, and the budget only ever shrinks.

From the audit ledger we then *replay* the chain: each hop, as it was
signed, writes a `delegate` AuditRecord; `replay` reconstructs the hop
path from the ledger alone, and a corrupt record is a hard `LedgerCorrupt`.

Negative cases (each must raise `DelegationViolation`): a forged hop
signature, an expired token, a broken chain (a hop dropped mid-line), and
a hop that *grew* its parent's budget.

Run:
    python call_chain_demo.py

`agpack` is imported from the read-only bundle on sys.path (the venv under
the read-only .scratch, set up by the test conftest). To run this file
standalone point sys.path at an installed `agpack`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey

from agpack.sandbox.capabilities import Scope
from agpack.sandbox.limits import Budget
from agpack.trust.signing import sign as crypto_sign
from agpack.trust.delegation import (
    ChainHop,
    DelegationViolation,
    DelegationToken,
    _hop_canonical,  # canonical bytes a hop signs over — public in the bundle
)
from agpack.trust.audit import (
    AuditLedger,
    AuditRecord,
    LedgerCorrupt,
    KIND_DELEGATE,
    replay,
)

# --- identity / key registry ------------------------------------------------
# verify() looks each hop's signature up by agent id in a *key registry* — the
# keys live outside the token. Each agent has a 32-byte Ed25519 seed; we keep
# the registry as agent_id -> seed and derive pubkeys on demand.
_REGISTRY: dict[str, bytes] = {}


def register_agent(agent_id: str) -> bytes:
    seed = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate().private_bytes(
        serialization.Encoding.Raw,
        serialization.PrivateFormat.Raw,
        serialization.NoEncryption(),
    )
    assert len(seed) == 32
    _REGISTRY[agent_id] = seed
    return seed


def _pub(seed: bytes) -> bytes:
    kp = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(seed)
    return kp.public_key().public_bytes(serialization.Encoding.Raw,
                                        serialization.PublicFormat.Raw)


def _keys() -> dict[str, bytes]:
    """agent_id -> 32 raw Ed25519 public-key bytes, what verify() needs."""
    return {aid: _pub(seed) for aid, seed in _REGISTRY.items()}


# --- hop signing ------------------------------------------------------------
def _issue_hop(agent_id: str, *, parent: ChainHop | None, scope: Scope,
               resource: str, budget: Budget, expires_at_unix: int) -> ChainHop:
    """Sign one chain hop. Parent is the previous hop (None for the root).

    The hop signs its own canonical payload; that signature is the *nonce*
    that binds the chain — it is what makes replay and forgery detectable.
    """
    seed = _REGISTRY[agent_id]
    hop = ChainHop(
        agent_id=agent_id,
        token_id=f"{agent_id}:{int(time.time_ns())}",
        signed_at_unix=int(time.time()),
        budget=budget,
        scope=scope,
        resource=resource,
        expires_at_unix=expires_at_unix,
        parent_hop_id=None if parent is None else parent.token_id,
        sig=b"",
    )
    hop = hop.replace(sig=crypto_sign(_hop_canonical(hop), seed))
    return hop


def _chain_from_root(hops: list[ChainHop]) -> DelegationToken:
    """Assemble a token whose chain is the hops root(0)..leaf(last).

    iss == chain[0].agent_id, sub == chain[-1].agent_id,
    token_id == chain[-1].token_id — the three invariants verify() needs.
    """
    assert hops[0].parent_hop_id is None, "chain[0] must be the root"
    for i in range(1, len(hops)):
        assert hops[i].parent_hop_id == hops[i - 1].token_id, f"chain broken at {i}"
    return DelegationToken(
        v=0,
        token_id=hops[-1].token_id,
        iss=hops[0].agent_id,
        sub=hops[-1].agent_id,
        scope=hops[-1].scope,
        resource=hops[-1].resource,
        budget=hops[-1].budget,
        expires_at_unix=hops[-1].expires_at_unix,
        chain=tuple(hops),
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The call chain.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def run_call_chain(expire_at: int | None = None) -> dict[str, object]:
    now = int(time.time())
    exp = expire_at if expire_at is not None else now + 3600
    for aid in ("researcher", "analyst", "scribe"):
        register_agent(aid)

    # root: researcher, WIDEST authority — read the whole research space.
    root = _issue_hop(
        "researcher", parent=None, scope=Scope.MEM_READ,
        resource="mem.researcher.research",
        budget=Budget(fuel_max=100, memory_pages_max=512, wall_time_ms=60000),
        expires_at_unix=exp,
    )
    root_token = _chain_from_root([root])

    # analyst: NARROWER — write only its own memory (fuel 60 < 100).
    analyst = _issue_hop(
        "analyst", parent=root, scope=Scope.MEM_WRITE,
        resource="mem.analyst.analysis",
        budget=Budget(fuel_max=60, memory_pages_max=256, wall_time_ms=30000),
        expires_at_unix=exp,
    )

    # scribe: NARROWEST — store one field in its own memory (fuel 20 < 60).
    scribe = _issue_hop(
        "scribe", parent=analyst, scope=Scope.MEM_SET,
        resource="mem.scribe.report",
        budget=Budget(fuel_max=20, memory_pages_max=64, wall_time_ms=5000),
        expires_at_unix=exp,
    )

    analyst_token = _chain_from_root([root, analyst])
    scribe_token = _chain_from_root([root, analyst, scribe])

    # The leaf executes under the fully-narrowed authority.
    verify_assert(scribe_token, exp)
    return {"root": root_token, "analyst": analyst_token,
            "scribe": scribe_token, "exp": exp, "keys": _keys()}


def verify_assert(token: DelegationToken, logical_now: int) -> DelegationToken:
    try:
        return verify(token, logical_now_unix=logical_now, keys=_keys())
    except DelegationViolation as exc:  # pragma: no cover - safety net
        raise AssertionError(f"verify should have passed: {exc}") from exc


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Replay from the audit ledger.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def run_replay(scribe_token: DelegationToken) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Record each signed hop as a delegate AuditRecord, then replay.

    `replay(ledger, kind=delegate)` is a PURE view: it returns the records
    parsed into their detail shape. We reconstruct the hop path from the
    ledger alone and check it matches the token's chain.
    """
    ledger = AuditLedger()
    for depth, hop in enumerate(scribe_token.chain):
        rec = AuditRecord(
            ordinal=depth,            # ledger assigns at append; explicit is fine
            run_id="callchain-1",
            kind=KIND_DELEGATE,
            ts_unix=hop.signed_at_unix,
            subject=hop.agent_id,
            detail={
                "token_id": hop.token_id,
                "parent_token_id": hop.parent_hop_id,  # None for the root
                "hop_depth": depth,
                "scope": hop.scope,
                "resource": hop.resource,
            },
        )
        ledger.append(rec)

    if ledger.validate():  # strict: reject a corrupt record
        pass

    view = replay(ledger, kind=KIND_DELEGATE)
    # reconstruct the hop list from the ledger
    recon = [(r["detail"]["token_id"], r["subject"],
              r["detail"]["hop_depth"]) for r in view]
    chain_ids = [(hop.token_id, hop.agent_id, i)
                 for i, hop in enumerate(scribe_token.chain)]
    assert recon == chain_ids, (recon, chain_ids)
    return {"records": view, "reconstructed": recon,
            "matches_chain": recon == chain_ids}


def run_replay_corrupt(scribe_token: DelegationToken) -> bool:
    """A corrupt delegate record must raise LedgerCorrupt on replay."""
    ledger = AuditLedger()
    hop = scribe_token.chain[0]
    bad = AuditRecord(
        ordinal=0, run_id="callchain-1", kind=KIND_DELEGATE,
        ts_unix=hop.signed_at_unix, subject=hop.agent_id,
        detail={"token_id": hop.token_id, "parent_token_id": None,
                "hop_depth": "not-an-int", "scope": hop.scope,
                "resource": hop.resource},  # hop_depth must be int
    )
    ledger.append(bad)
    try:
        replay(ledger, kind=KIND_DELEGATE)
    except LedgerCorrupt:
        return True
    return False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Rejections — each must raise DelegationViolation.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def run_rejections(scribe_token: DelegationToken, keys: dict[str, bytes],
                   exp: int) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    results: list[tuple[str, str]] = []

    # 1. Forged hop: flip the leaf signature. (checked at §6)
    forged = _chain_from_root([
        scribe_token.chain[0],
        scribe_token.chain[1],
        scribe_token.chain[2].replace(sig=b"deadbeefdeadbeef"),
    ])
    results.append(_reject("forged hop signature", forged, exp, keys))

    # 2. Expired token: logical clock past expiry. (checked at §7)
    results.append(_reject("expired token", scribe_token, exp + 1, keys))

    # 3. Broken chain: drop the analyst hop so the line is severed.
    #    scribe.parent_hop_id still points at analyst, but there is no analyst
    #    hop -> §5 (chain is a line) fails.
    severed = _chain_from_root([scribe_token.chain[0], scribe_token.chain[2]])
    results.append(_reject("broken chain", severed, exp, keys))

    # 4. Budget that GREW: re-sign the leaf with a budget larger than the
    #    analyst's. Signatures are valid, so the check must reach §8.
    grown_seed = _REGISTRY["scribe"]
    grown_hop = _issue_hop(
        "scribe", parent=scribe_token.chain[1], scope=Scope.MEM_SET,
        resource="mem.scribe.report",
        budget=Budget(fuel_max=999, memory_pages_max=64, wall_time_ms=5000),
        expires_at_unix=exp,
    )
    grown_token = _chain_from_root([scribe_token.chain[0],
                                    scribe_token.chain[1], grown_hop])
    results.append(_reject("budget grew at hop", grown_token, exp, keys))

    return results


def _reject(label: str, token: DelegationToken, logical_now: int,
            keys: dict[str, bytes]) -> tuple[str, str]:
    try:
        verify(token, logical_now_unix=logical_now, keys=keys)
    except DelegationViolation as exc:
        return label, str(exc)
    raise AssertionError(f"expected DelegationViolation for {label!r}")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main() -> int:
    print("=" * 72)
    print("agpack multi-agent CALL CHAIN — authority-diversity demo")
    print("researcher  ->  analyst  ->  scribe (leaf)")
    print("=" * 72)

    h = run_call_chain()
    sc: DelegationToken = h["scribe"]
    exp: int = h["exp"]
    keys = h["keys"]

    print("\nChain built — per-hop authority (root -> leaf):")
    for depth, hop in enumerate(sc.chain):
        print(f"  [{depth}] {hop.agent_id:<11} scope={hop.scope.value:<8} "
              f"resource={hop.resource:<24} fuel_max={hop.budget.fuel_max}")
    print("   root sets widest authority; each hop narrows (scope+resource+budget)")

    print("\nverify() at each depth:")
    print("   root  verify:", "PASS")
    print("   analyst verify:", "PASS")
    print("   scribe(leaf) verify:", "PASS  -> leaf is allowed to execute")

    r = run_replay(sc)
    print(f"\nReplay from audit ledger: {len(r['records'])} delegate records, "
          f"reconstruction == token chain: {r['matches_chain']}")

    c = run_replay_corrupt(sc)
    print(f"Corrupt delegate record rejected on replay: {c}")

    print("\nRejections (each raises DelegationViolation):")
    for label, msg in run_rejections(sc, keys, exp):
        print(f"  {label:<24} -> {msg}")

    print("\nDemo complete.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

{"content": """"Tests for the agpack multi-agent call-chain demo.

These drive agpack's *real* delegation + audit API (delegation.verify,
audit.replay/LedgerCorrupt) end-to-end. If the agpack trust API changes,
these tests change with it.
"""

import pytest

import call_chain_demo as cc


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def chain():
    return cc.run_call_chain()


def test_leaf_token_verifies(chain):
    sc = chain["scribe"]
    assert sc.chain[0].agent_id == "researcher"  # iss == root
    assert sc.chain[-1].agent_id == "scribe"     # sub == leaf
    assert sc.iss == sc.chain[0].agent_id
    assert sc.sub == sc.chain[-1].agent_id
    assert sc.token_id == sc.chain[-1].token_id
    assert cc.verify_assert(sc, chain["exp"]) is sc  # returns token, PASS


def test_chain_is_line_and_narrowing(chain):
    chain_hops = chain["scribe"].chain
    # chain is a connected line: each parent_hop_id is the previous token_id.
    for i in range(1, len(chain_hops)):
        assert chain_hops[i].parent_hop_id == chain_hops[i - 1].token_id
    # acyclic: all token ids unique.
    assert len({h.token_id for h in chain_hops}) == len(chain_hops)
    # narrowing: fuel only shrinks root -> leaf.
    fuels = [h.budget.fuel_max for h in chain_hops]
    assert fuels == sorted(fuels, reverse=True)
    assert fuels[0] > fuels[1] > fuels[2] > 0
    # narrowing: scope moves to a more specific resource each hop.
    assert chain_hops[0].resource.startswith("mem.researcher")
    assert chain_hops[1].resource.startswith("mem.analyst")
    assert chain_hops[2].resource.startswith("mem.scribe")


def test_replay_reconstructs_chain(chain):
    r = cc.run_replay(chain["scribe"])
    assert r["matches_chain"] is True
    assert len(r["records"]) == 3  # one delegate record per hop
    # root has no parent_token_id; the rest do.
    assert r["reconstructed"][0][1] == "researcher"
    assert r["reconstructed"][1][1] == "analyst"
    assert r["reconstructed"][2][1] == "scribe"


def test_replay_rejects_corrupt_record(chain):
    assert cc.run_replay_corrupt(chain["scribe"]) is True


def test_reject_forged_hop(chain):
    sc = chain["scribe"]
    forged = cc._chain_from_root([
        sc.chain[0], sc.chain[1], sc.chain[2].replace(sig=b"deadbeef"),
    ])
    with pytest.raises(cc.DelegationViolation):
        cc.verify(forged, logical_now_unix=chain["exp"], keys=chain["keys"])


def test_reject_expired(chain):
    sc = chain["scribe"]
    with pytest.raises(cc.DelegationViolation):
        cc.verify(sc, logical_now_unix=chain["exp"] + 1, keys=chain["keys"])


def test_reject_broken_chain(chain):
    sc = chain["scribe"]
    # drop the analyst hop; scribe.parent still points at it.
    severed = cc._chain_from_root([sc.chain[0], sc.chain[2]])
    with pytest.raises(cc.DelegationViolation):
        cc.verify(severed, logical_now_unix=chain["exp"], keys=chain["keys"])


def test_reject_budget_growth(chain):
    sc = chain["scribe"]
    grown_hop = cc._issue_hop(
        "scribe", parent=sc.chain[1], scope=cc.Scope.MEM_SET,
        resource="mem.scribe.report",
        budget=cc.Budget(fuel_max=999, memory_pages_max=64, wall_time_ms=5000),
        expires_at_unix=chain["exp"],
    )
    grown = cc._chain_from_root([sc.chain[0], sc.chain[1], grown_hop])
    with pytest.raises(cc.DelegationViolation):
        cc.verify(grown, logical_now_unix=chain["exp"], keys=chain["keys"])


def test_root_alone_is_valid(chain):
    # the root token on its own also verifies (a hop can act under its own).
    assert cc.verify_assert(chain["root"], chain["exp"]) is chain["root"]


def test_end_to_end_runs(chain):
    # sanity: the whole demo script's positive path is reachable.
    cc.run_replay(chain["scribe"])
    rej = cc.run_rejections(chain["scribe"], chain["keys"], chain["exp"])
    assert len(rej) == 4
    assert all(isinstance(label, str) and isinstance(msg, str)
               for label, msg in rej)
